title: Tape of plans found in Toronto hostage-taker's car
article: A man who was shot and killed by Toronto police on Wednesday as he held a woman hostage left an audiotape allegedly detailing plans to kill his estranged wife, according to reports.
The Special Investigations Unit confirmed they found the tape in the back of Anthony Brookes' minivan and that it is now part of their probe.
Brookes reportedly blamed his actions on his wife Marlene, saying "you made me do this, you drove me to it."

Brookes, 45, had a history of domestic violence. He had abused his wife, 16-year-old son and 18-year-old daughter, who last March left their home in Ajax, Ont., to move to a secret location in west Toronto.
Brookes had been convicted in May for assaulting his wife and daughter and was sentenced to 30 days in jail.
According to court documents, Brookes beat his wife, pushed her down the stairs, held a knife to her throat, punched and choked her.
He also threatened his daughter with a knife and beat her.
Following his release, he was subject to a restraining order to stay away from his family, and barred from possessing any kind of weapons.
Marlene had recently initiated divorce proceedings against him.
On Wednesday, Brookes was killed by a police sniper's bullet after taking a woman hostage outside Toronto's Union Station.
The ordeal began minutes earlier when Brookes had confronted Marlene at a nearby food court. He fired several shots at her but missed.
She tripped and fell trying to get away. Brookes went over to her and began pistol whipping her. He then fled the scene.
Marlene is still recovering in hospital from head injuries.
A police officer in the area heard about the details of the shootings and caught up with Brookes outside the Fairmont Royal York Hotel.
Brookes ran to Union Station where he grabbed 20-year-old Nicole Regis.
The standoff lasted for about half an hour before police shot and killed Brookes about 8:50 a.m.
